title: Leadership Brightens the Collective Path
author: Kathleen Schafer
summary: Schafer restates the foundation of her work, that leadership is love in action, and argues that care has been wrongly treated as a commodity rather than a public good. Drawing on a college political economy course, she holds that turning goods meant to be stewarded into profit centers does harm. She asks whether people can be compensated for caring without an extra layer of profit that drains those they serve. The piece frames this as a tipping point where leaders can put care back at the center of their work, and it ends with reflection questions in her usual style.
points: Leadership is defined as love in action: small, steady acts of encouragement, patience, truth and integrity that accumulate into influence for the whole.
The key claim is that care is a public good to be stewarded, not a commodity to be monetized.
Commodifying education, health care and similar goods is presented as extracting from the conditions that sustain shared wellbeing.
She poses a practical question for leaders: how can caring work be paid without a profit layer that drains those being served.
quotes: Light does not arrive with fanfare. It grows through small acts of kindness that ripple outward until they become illumination.
we have been treating care as a commodity rather than what it truly is, a public good.

it does harm to turn public goods into profit centers. Goods that help society function and thrive, education, health care, infrastructure, clean air, safe water are not meant to be exploited. They are meant to be stewarded.
We have blurred the line between what is meant to be purchased and what is meant to be provided.
If leadership is love in action, then caring must return to the center of our world.
There is no price tag on genuine care. Without it, our world becomes hollow and gray.
